Definition: from G2596 and a derivative of the same as G4195; to plunge down, i.e. submerge:--drown, sink.
BiblicalUsage: Peter saw the wind and was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried, Lord, save me, and Jesus warns that whoever offends one of these little ones should be sunk in the depth of the sea with a millstone about his neck.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Peter's sinking is my story too, because fear takes my eyes off Jesus, and His hand is still there to catch me.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
